# Basics: status, doctor, version, help, login, logout

The commands that are a whole domain. `orca status` first when anything looks wrong.

## `orca status`

one screen: is the panel answering, and the facts around it (read-only, starts nothing)

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: anyone; runs here, needs no panel.
- Exit codes: 0 every check ok (warnings allowed); 1 a check failed.

```
orca status
orca status --json
```

## `orca doctor`

status's checks plus slower ones (agent CLIs on the service PATH, ~/.orca modes, stale sockets), with one fix line per failure (read-only)

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: anyone; runs here, needs no panel.
- Exit codes: 0 every check ok (warnings allowed); 1 a check failed.

```
orca doctor
```

## `orca version`

the CLI's version (the orca-control skill's version: should equal it)

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: anyone; runs here, needs no panel.

```
orca version
orca version --json
```

## `orca login --name <name>`

store a person token for this terminal: the panel account's password, typed here; used only with --as-person

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `--name <name>` (required): the panel account to log in as

```
orca login --name ana
orca usage set-cap --scope all --period week --tokens 500000 --as-person
```

## `orca logout`

revoke the stored person token and remove it

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).

```
orca logout
```

## `orca help [<topic>...]`

this list, or one domain's or one command's help

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: anyone; runs here, needs no panel.
- `<topic>` (optional) (one or more): a domain, or a domain and an action

```
orca help
orca help group
orca help group start
```
